newsitem.title: UK: NatWest Markets gets new chief, shake-up.
newsitem.headline: NatWest Markets gets new chief, shake-up.

text.p: National Westminster Bank on Friday said it had appointed Konrad "Chip" Kruger as the new chief executive of its investment bank NatWest Markets.

At the same time, NatWest said it was removing the Treasury, Foreign Exchange, Interest Rate Trading, Money Markets and Currency Options functions from Markets and putting them in a new Global Financial Markets section within the Group structure.
NatWest was expected to announce the review of its investment banking activities next week when it announces its half-year results.
Kruger is currently co-chief executive of Global Debt Markets and was a senior executive in Greenwich Capital, the U.S. bond house bought by NatWest Markets last year.
NatWest said its group chief executive Derek Wanless, who has been running NatWest Markets since the resignation of its former head Martin Owen, will become its chairman.

Owen resigned and the review of Markets' operations was begun after it emerged that the business had lost 90 million pounds ($147 million) on interest rate options trading. The losses had been covered up, the bank later admitted, and several other senior managers also resigned.

The appointment of Kruger is likely to be viewed as defensive. Analysts said the appointment of an insider meant the NatWest management had been unable to sell the appointment to any hard-hitting outsider.
Outgoing Securities and Investments Board (SIB) chairman Sir Andrew Large had been mentioned as a possible candidate in the press.

Analysts said the changes in structure were largely cosmetic but would increase the options for the NatWest management. The removal of the Treasury from the Markets business, for example, would make NatWest Markets easier to sell if the bank ever wished to.
NatWest said the Markets division would now focus on investment banking activities in equities, debt markets and corporate advisory.
It said the changes would free 4.0 billion pounds of weighted risk assets this year and 6.0 billion in 1998 from a starting position of 31 billion.
